speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me if this baby was born prematurely or via a C-section?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the baby was born at 33 weeks, has a history of uneventful prenatal care, and is now showing respiratory distress two hours after birth, I suspect this might be transient tachypnea of the newborn. REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L; Chest Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood gas shows respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia, and the chest X-ray reveals fine reticular granulation with a ground glass appearance. These findings are classic for Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN).

DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN)
